items.what: An optional human acceptance of each change's working behaviour, recorded against the exact tree that merges (`approval.acceptance` in .gates.yaml).
items.question: Should a human accept each change's working behaviour before it merges?

options.label: Yes, I accept my own changes: `acceptance: self` (Recommended)
Yes, a reviewer accepts on the pull request: `acceptance: review` (needs `integration.mode: pull-request`)
No acceptance step: a change merges once its gates are green, as today

items.what: Who writes a change's failing tests: a separate test-author agent, once per change before the first task, or the implementer itself under the same lock (`loop.test-author` in .gates.yaml).
items.question: Who should write each change's tests?

options.label: A separate test author, before implementation starts: `test-author: separate` (Recommended)
The implementer writes them itself, bound by the same lock: `test-author: inline`
Leave it unset: the default, `separate`, applies

items.what: Your project's own test rules (`Applies to: tests` in the rules-doc), which the test author writes to and the reviewer checks. Without them, new tests follow only the built-in rule and can read as foreign to the project.
items.question: Capture this project's test conventions now, from the material it already has?

options.label: Capture them now; I confirm each rule before it is written (Recommended)
No: the test author follows the built-in rule only

items.what: The runner behind a blocking gate must fail on an undefined test and must not retry a failure to green; only its own configuration can guarantee that.
items.question: Have you checked that the runners behind your blocking gates fail on an undefined or skipped test and never retry a failure to green?

options.label: Yes, I have checked them (Recommended)
No, and don't ask again: I accept that a gate may pass on an undefined or retried test

action.detail: gatedloop cannot read runner flags out of a command string without naming a stack, so this is yours to honour in each bound runner's own configuration. A blocking gate's runner must: (1) fail on an undefined test, or on one skipped because its implementation is missing; (2) not retry a failure until it passes, because a retry that passes hides a flaky test on a blocking path; (3) keep checks whose verdict depends on a model's reply under the advisory `eval` gate. Check the commands bound to `verify`, `integration` and each surface's `live-check`.

items.what: A project-local schema can declare `gatedloop: { flow: regression-first }`, so the loop runs a failing reproduction red before any fix instead of the default per-task loop.
items.question: Review this project's local schemas for the regression-first flow now?

options.label: Review them now (Recommended)
No: every local schema keeps the default per-task flow

action.detail: /gatedloop:tdd-apply routes a schema by its structure and what it declares, never by its name (`gates schema dispatch <name>`). A schema with an `apply:` block that has `tracks` runs the per-task loop unless it declares a top-level `gatedloop:` key with `flow: regression-first`; then the failing reproduction must run red before any fix, as in the bundled bugfix pack. Name each schema under openspec/schemas/ and the route `gates schema dispatch` gives it; declaring the key in a schema is the adopter's own edit to that schema.

items.what: An optional `confirm` gate that brings the merged tree up on your own environment and smoke-checks it, which `gates merge` runs before anything is pushed (`gates.confirm` in .gates.yaml).
items.question: This project binds a live-check. Should `gates merge` also smoke-check the merged tree with a `confirm` gate before it pushes?

options.label: Yes, bind a confirm gate now through onboarding's confirm offer (Recommended)
No: the merge skips its confirm step with a note, as today

items.what: A git-layer hook in this repository (`pre-commit` or `pre-push`) is a direct copy of an earlier (or locally edited) gatedloop template, or the shim path it records is gone, so it does not run the shipped check. A refresh replaces the copy and keeps the old body beside it as `<hook>.gatedloop-prev`.
items.question: Refresh the git-layer hooks to the templates this gatedloop version ships?

options.label: Refresh them now; each old body is kept as `<hook>.gatedloop-prev` (Recommended)
Not at this version: keep the installed copy, which does not run the shipped check

items.what: An active change's `.openspec.yaml` still carries gatedloop's approval keys in the earlier spelling (`approved_by`, `approved_at`, `approved_sha`). OpenSpec 1.14 reports them as unrecognized and `openspec validate --strict` fails on them; it ignores keys starting with `x-`, which is where gatedloop 0.5.1 writes them.
items.question: Rename the approval keys in this project's active changes to the `x-gatedloop-approved-*` spelling?

options.label: Rename them now with `gates approval migrate`, then commit the result (Recommended)
Not at this version: keep the earlier spelling, which gatedloop still reads but `openspec validate --strict` fails on

action.detail: Run `gates approval migrate`. It renames `approved_by`, `approved_at` and `approved_sha` to `x-gatedloop-approved-by`, `x-gatedloop-approved-at` and `x-gatedloop-approved-sha` in each active change's `.openspec.yaml`, keeping the values, and prints each file it changed. The approval sha covers no `.openspec.yaml`, so every approval still checks. It does not commit: commit the files it names (a planning-grade commit). Archived changes are left alone.

items.what: The loop's stopping rule is now enforced from the ledger: after a task's RED run it gets `loop.attempts` failed `unit` or `ci` runs (default 2), then `gates run` refuses that task's next run. One fresh restart per task (`loop.fresh-restarts`, default 1) is allowed first, in a new agent context that reads only the task's attempt notes, before a human gets it.
items.question: How many failed attempts should a task get before the loop stops, with one fresh restart before a human?

options.label: Keep the defaults, 2 failed attempts then 1 fresh restart: `attempts: 2` (Recommended)
A larger budget: `attempts: 3`; edit it afterwards to set your own
Leave it unset: the defaults apply; to disable restarts, set `loop.fresh-restarts: 0` by hand

items.what: Your `.claude/settings.local.json` asks on `Bash(git merge *)`, the rule earlier permission scaffolding wrote. Every `git merge` an agent issues then prompts, including a lane's routine sync of the target into its own change branch, and an unattended lane stalls on a prompt nobody answers. Integration now goes through `gates merge` (or the forge), so the human checkpoint belongs there.
items.question: Move the permission checkpoint from every `git merge` to `gates merge`?

options.label: Yes: I replace `Bash(git merge *)` with `Bash(gates merge *)` in `permissions.ask` (Recommended)
Not at this version: keep asking on every `git merge`, and accept that unattended lanes stall on a sync

action.detail: In `.claude/settings.local.json`, under `permissions.ask`, replace `"Bash(git merge *)"` with `"Bash(gates merge *)"`, leaving every other rule as it is. This is the adopter's own one-line edit; gatedloop never changes a permission file without an explicit yes. The merge hook still gates a raw integration `git merge` into the target, and `gates merge`, the command that integrates, still always asks. The change takes effect in a new session.

items.what: This project still uses the plugin's earlier name, Specloop: a `.specloop/` state directory, `x-specloop-*` keys in an active change, or `specloop` markers in its git pre-commit hook. They are read, with a warning, until 0.8.0.
items.question: Move this project onto the gatedloop names now?

options.label: Yes: I run `gates migrate-name`, commit what it changed, and make the edits it prints (Recommended)
Not at this version: keep the earlier names, which stop working in 0.8.0

action.detail: Run `gates migrate-name` from the repository root. It moves `.specloop/` to `.gatedloop/` with `git mv`, renames the `x-specloop-*` keys in each active change's `.openspec.yaml` (values kept; the approval sha covers no `.openspec.yaml`, so every approval still checks), renames the markers in a composed git hook, and leaves archived changes alone. It commits nothing: commit what it changed. It then prints the edits it does not make, each with its replacement: the Claude Code plugin install, any permission rule or setting naming the earlier plugin, and branch protection requiring `specloop/ci`, which can wait because both contexts are posted until 0.8.0.

items.what: gatedloop now ships a git `pre-push` hook beside the commit hook. Inside a declared agent session (`discipline.agent-env`, default `CLAUDECODE`) it denies a push that updates the merge target unless the pushed commit is proven: a `merge` ledger row records it, as `gates merge` writes, or the merge gate's incoming-tree checks hold for its tree. Without it, a raw merge of the target pushed by hand reaches the shared history unchecked. Other branches, deletions and human pushes are untouched.
items.question: Install the git pre-push hook that gates a push of the merge target?

options.label: Yes: install the push hook with `gates hook install` (Recommended)
No: keep the commit hook only; a raw merge pushed by hand stays unchecked locally
